purpose: Evidence-native verification, validation, reproducibility, traceability, and mission assurance for high-consequence frontier systems.
public_release_policy: The public repository contains software, schemas, source-neutral reference fixtures, documentation, and release evidence. Mission-specific and protected evidence remains in governed environments.

list unresolved assumptions without automated priority scoring
expose direct evidence gaps on critical nodes
show dependency impact through declared depends_on/requires relations
verify declared code and input artifact hashes plus versioned output acceptance and numerical checks
reproduce trusted version-2 receipts and local version-3 receipts in a fresh declared-artifact workspace with SHA-256-bound code, direct declared-entrypoint execution, and freshly generated outputs
verify version-3.1 exact, semantic, record-only, and hybrid output assurance while preserving an observed SHA-256 for every output
validate version-3.1 external execution chronology and calibration coverage over the declared execution interval
bind synthetic external-job submission and collection provenance for portable verification
scan every Git-tracked release file before public release eligibility
verify that decision-receipt basis references exist in a valid graph
validate portable scientific-discovery assurance contracts and their synthetic cross-record references
keep formal proof-checker state separate from specification-equivalence state
preserve explicit research-priority, research-boundary, attribution, and replication states
connect consequential decisions to explicit reopen conditions through Mission Decision Packets
validate Orbital Recovery Assurance contracts and source-neutral cross-record invariants
project a Mission Recovery Chain across power, contact, telemetry, command, and capability while keeping trust and authority cross-cutting
assess robust recovery-option eligibility under declared models
validate governed local orbital-recovery case structure without moving mission evidence into the public repository
preserve post-intervention requalification and Time-to-Trust evidence as distinct from technical restoration
publish stable identifiers for versioned portable contracts
governed_externally: safety, security, acquisition, compliance, and mission-readiness approval
mission-specific evidence custody and access control
trusted execution environments for code requiring isolation beyond FMA integrity controls
authorship authentication and trust-root policy for unsigned core receipts
specification equivalence for formal scientific or engineering claims
distribution: GitHub source and stable release workflow; public package-index upload is intentionally blocked by package metadata. Assurance profiles are distributed in the repository/source archive while the core wheel carries the frontier_assurance package and CLI.
evidence_lifecycle: Source-controlled validation defines deterministic expectations; commit-specific hosted proof belongs to GitHub Actions and tagged release metadata.
interoperability: Versioned core schemas use stable identifiers. Richer domain records map into FMA contracts through explicit adapters while preserving local evidence, calibration, acceptance, and decision semantics.
maintenance: Keep main as the protected long-lived branch, use immutable GitHub Action pins, dependency review, protected-main CodeQL, reviewed dependency updates, tracked-file public-release scanning, and full V&V after material source changes.
